overview.title: About NKS WebDev Console
overview.body:
NKS WebDev Console manages a local development environment on Windows, macOS and Linux. It replaces MAMP, XAMPP and Laragon with one interface for Apache, Nginx, PHP, MySQL, MariaDB, Redis, Mailpit, Composer, SSL (mkcert) and Cloudflare Tunnels.

Services run in a separate background process (the daemon); the app window is just the control panel. Switch between Simple and Advanced mode in the header. Simple shows only the essentials, Advanced adds databases, binaries, plugins and more tools.

firstSite.title: Create your first site
firstSite.body:
Open Sites in the left menu and click New site (or press Ctrl+N). Enter a local domain (e.g. myapp.loc) and choose the site folder. WDC adds the domain to the hosts file for you.

Simple mode

A short form: domain, site folder, PHP version and optional HTTPS and Cloudflare Tunnel.

Advanced mode

A table of sites and the full configuration of each site in tabs: General, Runtime, Cloudflare, SSL, Composer, Metrics, Errors, History and Danger.

sitesSimple.title: Sites — Simple Mode
sitesSimple.body:
Simple mode shows a card for each site with start/stop, open-in-browser and quick settings. Create a site with the + New Site button.

Setup

Domain + document root (auto-suggested from C:\work\sites\<domain>), PHP version picker, Cloudflare Tunnel toggle, SSL toggle.

sitesAdvanced.title: Sites — Advanced Mode
sitesAdvanced.body:
Table view. Primary row action is Edit (opens SiteEdit with full 9-tab configuration); Open-in-browser, Detect framework, Delete live in the row overflow menu.

SiteEdit tabs

  • General — domain, aliases, document root, PHP version
  • Runtime — PHP-FPM pool tuning, environment variables
  • Cloudflare — per-site tunnel config
  • SSL — per-site cert switch + path overrides
  • Composer — package manager
  • Metrics — request rate, historical traffic chart
  • Errors — aggregated Apache + PHP-FPM error tail
  • History — config rollback points
  • Danger — rename domain / delete

databases.title: Databases
databases.body:
Manage MySQL / MariaDB databases at /databases. List, create, drop; run ad-hoc SQL queries; import / export SQL dumps.

Troubleshooting

If the page shows "ERROR 1045 Access denied" the WDC-managed MySQL port (3306 by default) is occupied by MAMP / XAMPP. Fix: Settings → Ports → change MySQL port, or stop the external service.

ssl.title: SSL certificates
ssl.body:
/ssl manages locally-trusted TLS certs via mkcert.

Setup

  • Install CA — mkcert root into the system trust store. Runs once per machine.
  • Generate — issue a cert for a domain + optional aliases.

Cert status

Each cert card shows expiry countdown (badge turns amber ≤ 14 days), issuer DN, SHA1 fingerprint. Orphan certs (no matching site) are dimmed with an Orphan badge.

composer.title: Composer
composer.body:
Per-site Composer management lives on SiteEdit → Composer tab and globally on /composer.

  • Auto-discovers composer.phar under ~/.wdc/binaries/composer/.
  • Install / Require / Remove / Diagnose / Outdated run through the plugin invoker (no shell interpolation).
  • Hover a package name to see Packagist metadata popover.

cloudflare.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
cloudflare.body:
/cloudflare exposes WDC sites to a public URL via Cloudflare Tunnel — no firewall port opening needed.

Setup

Paste your Cloudflare API token + pick a zone. Per-site: enable the Tunnel switch on SiteEdit → Cloudflare.

Note: cloudflared is a single process routing ALL tunneled sites. Restarting it affects the entire tunnel fleet.

hosts.title: Hosts file
hosts.body:
/hosts is a safer editor for the system hosts file. WDC-managed entries live inside a BEGIN NKS WebDev Console / END NKS WebDev Console marker block — anything outside is preserved verbatim.

Safety

Requires administrator privileges on Windows. Apply creates a timestamped .bak backup before each write.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.body:
WDC is plugin-driven. The daemon loads IWdcPlugin assemblies from the plugin dir (Apache, MySQL, PHP, Redis, Composer, SSL, Cloudflare…). Each plugin is independently versioned.

Writing a plugin: see PLUGIN-API.md and the WRITING-A-PLUGIN walkthrough.

mcp.title: MCP dev API
mcp.body:
WDC ships an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server so AI dev tools (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.) can automate site creation and management.

Available tools

  • wdc_create_site
  • wdc_list_databases
  • wdc_generate_cert
  • wdc_cloudflare_config

The MCP server runs as a separate service in the daemon process. Point your MCP-compatible tool at the nks-wdc transport.

shortcuts.title: Keyboard shortcuts
shortcuts.body:
• Ctrl+K / Cmd+K: open the command palette (works with Caps Lock and on any keyboard layout)
  • F5: reconnect to the daemon
  • Ctrl+N: new site
  • Ctrl+1 to Ctrl+7: Overview / Sites / Databases / SSL / PHP / Binaries / Settings. The numbers are the top-row keys and work without Shift on a Czech keyboard. In Simple mode they also open pages the menu does not list.

While you type in a text field or the editor, shortcuts other than Ctrl+K are ignored so they cannot take you away mid-edit.

settings.title: Settings
settings.body:
/settings covers:

  • General — language, theme, UI mode, run on startup, auto-start services, default PHP version, telemetry.
  • Ports — override ports for each managed service.
  • Paths — override binary paths + hosts file path.
  • Databases — default MySQL admin credentials.
  • Advanced — plugin toggles, service auto-restart, catalog URL override.
  • Account — optional sync to wdc-catalog-api.
  • Update — check for new WDC releases.
  • About — version, sources, runtime info.

binaries.title: Binaries
binaries.body:
/binaries manages runtime binaries (Apache, Nginx, PHP, MySQL, MariaDB, Redis, Caddy, Mailpit, cloudflared, mkcert, Node, Composer). Each is downloaded on-demand from GitHub releases matching your OS + arch. SHA-256 is verified before unpacking.

Upgrading

Upgrade in-place keeps older versions on disk as a rollback target.

metrics.title: Metrics + logs
metrics.body:
Each site has request metrics from the Apache access log and an error summary from Apache and PHP-FPM. Find them under Edit site → Metrics and Errors.

Overview

The Overview page sums up the state in one sentence, then lists Needs attention (a crashed service, missing Apache, an old backup, a new version), a table of services with status, port, version and CPU and memory use, and recent activity. Advanced mode adds CPU and memory charts for the last 5 minutes.

A service that is not installed is marked Not installed and has an Install button that opens the Binaries page.

mcpCapabilities.intro: AI clients connected over MCP may always read the state of WDC and do the everyday things listed below. Each group allows something more. Irreversible actions still need your approval in an enabled group, unless a rule covers them.
mcpCapabilities.loadFailed: Could not load the MCP capabilities: {err}
mcpCapabilities.approvalStillRequired: Irreversible actions still need your approval
mcpCapabilities.alwaysTitle: What an AI may always do
mcpCapabilities.alwaysHint: The MCP tools need this for everyday work. Only turning MCP off stops it.
mcpCapabilities.neverTitle: What an AI may never do
mcpCapabilities.enableConfirm: AI clients connected to WDC will be allowed to: {name}. Irreversible actions in this group still need your approval.
mcpCapabilities.mcpOff: MCP is off and the daemon refuses AI clients. Turn it on with the switch below.

settings_operator.title: Operator settings
settings_operator.description: Change deploy, daemon, plugin, sync, path and telemetry settings and the backup folder.

service_config.title: Service configuration
service_config.description: Overwrite httpd.conf, php.ini and other service configuration files. Each write needs your approval.

hosts_file.title: Hosts file
hosts_file.description: Rewrite, back up or restore the system hosts file. Writes need your approval.

node_process.title: Node.js processes
node_process.description: Set the start command of Node.js sites and start, stop and restart those processes. Starting needs your approval.

site_advanced_fields.title: Advanced site fields
site_advanced_fields.description: Set site fields beyond domain, folder, PHP and HTTPS (ports, environment, PHP settings).

cloudflare_credentials.title: Cloudflare credentials
cloudflare_credentials.description: Set the cloudflared path, tunnel and API tokens, the account and tunnel routing. Each change needs your approval.

plugin_install.title: Plugin installation
plugin_install.description: Install plugins from a URL and uninstall them. Each action needs your approval.

database_admin.title: Database server administration
database_admin.description: Reset and change the MySQL and PostgreSQL root passwords, drop MySQL accounts, create accounts with admin rights or for a non-local host, import SQL dumps and export to a file. Most of it needs your approval.

backup_restore.title: Backup restore and delete
backup_restore.description: Restore WDC from a backup over the current sites and settings, or delete a backup. Each action needs your approval.

deploy_config.title: Deploy configuration
deploy_config.description: Read and change the deploy settings of sites (servers, hooks, webhooks, environment variables), test hooks and notifications, check servers.

daemon_admin.title: Daemon administration
daemon_admin.description: Restart, shut down or reset the daemon and start the uninstall. Each action needs your approval.

unlisted_routes.title: Everything else
unlisted_routes.description: Every other daemon route not in a group above (Docker Compose, catalog sync and more).

composer.title: Composer
composer.description: Run Composer install, require and remove in site folders; package scripts run.

cloudflare_dns.title: Cloudflare DNS records
cloudflare_dns.description: Create public DNS records in the zones of the saved Cloudflare account, for example a subdomain pointing elsewhere. Deleting a record needs your approval either way.

neverList: Create, change or delete auto-approval rules.
Change MCP settings, including the switches on this page.
mcpCapabilities.riskyConfirm: "{name}" opens every daemon route not in another group to AI clients, including ones added later. To confirm, type {word}.
alwaysList: Read the state of WDC, sites, services, databases, logs, backups and settings.
Create, edit and delete sites and apply their configuration. Deleting a site needs your approval.
Start services. Stopping and restarting need your approval.
Create databases, read and export data and run read-only queries. Dropping a database and SQL that changes data need your approval.
Create MySQL accounts for an ordinary database and change their privileges. Resetting an account password needs your approval.
Turn plugins and PHP extensions on and off, install and uninstall binaries. Installing a binary needs your approval.
Create SSL certificates and install the certificate authority. Deleting a certificate needs your approval.
Change ordinary WDC settings (not operator or MCP settings) and create backups.
Read Cloudflare zones, DNS records and tunnels. Deleting a DNS record needs your approval.
Start a deploy, rollback or snapshot restore, each only after your approval.

master.off: MCP is off. The daemon refuses every AI client, including one already running. The switches below apply once MCP is on.

claudeCode.title: Claude Code
claudeCode.where: Run once in a terminal. The server is then available in every project.

claudeDesktop.title: Claude Desktop
claudeDesktop.where: Into claude_desktop_config.json (Windows: %APPDATA%\Claude\, macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/; Claude Desktop also opens it under Settings → Developer → Edit Config). If it already lists other servers, add only the nks-wdc entry to mcpServers. Then restart Claude Desktop.

cursor.title: Cursor
cursor.where: Into .cursor/mcp.json in the project, or ~/.cursor/mcp.json for every project. If it already lists other servers, add only the nks-wdc entry to mcpServers.
